Incongruent

/in-KONG-groo-uhnt/ - the stress falls on KONG · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incongruent means out of keeping — the formal word for things, such as tones or claims, that fail to fit each other.

A lullaby drifted over the mall's fire alarm, an incongruent pairing nobody at the help desk could explain.

Worked Example

Visitors kept sliding their headphones off in the memorial gallery: the audio guide's jokey, game-show patter was incongruent with a room built for grief.

Incongruent is the formal word for pieces that fail to fit — a tone against a setting, a claim against the evidence — and it usually travels with 'with.' Mismatched is its everyday cousin for concrete pairs: socks, gloves, chairs.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

mismatched: paired wrongly — the everyday word for socks and gloves

clashing: actively fighting each other, and loud about it

inconsistent: failing to agree from one statement or action to the next

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

matching: agreeing piece for piece

harmonious: fitting together into a pleasing whole

Where it sits · how sharply the two things clash — odd → incongruent → contradictory

odd vs. incongruent: Odd just means a little unexpected — it stops short of incongruent, where two things actively fail to fit together.

contradictory vs. incongruent: Contradictory goes further than incongruent: incongruent things sit badly together, while contradictory ones cannot both be true.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not

Root — -congru-

Root — -congru-: to come together, to agree (Latin congruere)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: adjective

Put it together

Put it together: A genuine 'not': in- + congruere ('to come together, to agree') + -ent. Congruent things meet point for point — geometry borrowed the word for triangles that coincide exactly — and incongruent things refuse the meeting.

Use the root in a new word: congruence

Use the root in a new word: congruence: The geometry proof ended by showing the congruence of the two triangles — a perfect point-for-point fit.

Word Choice

formal

Incongruent (and its twin incongruous) suits reports and reviews — tones, claims, designs out of keeping with their surroundings, usually incongruent with something named. For odd socks and clashing plaids, mismatched is the honest word.
